prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that at the Petersons' potluck, you presented a store-bought dish in your own cookware. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, members of the Committee:

I categorically deny the charge that I knowingly and willfully engaged in potluck misrepresentation.

It is true that the dish in question appeared in my own cookware. It is also true that the casserole—if we must use that term—was received from a commercial establishment. However, I submit that transfer to a Pyrex dish constitutes, at most, “plating,” not fraud. The American potluck tradition has always allowed room for improvisation, convenience, and strategic garnish.

I further wish to state for the record that I added fresh parsley, adjusted the lid foil, and allowed condensation to collect in a manner consistent with homemade preparation. These actions were undertaken not to deceive the Petersons, but to preserve communal morale.

At no point did I claim, under oath or over iced tea, that the dish was “from scratch.” When asked who made it, I responded, “Oh, it’s a little something I brought,” which is both legally and culinarily accurate.

I will not name the bakery. I will not implicate the deli counter. And I will not apologize for ensuring there was enough spinach-artichoke dip for all attendees.

In conclusion, I remain a loyal participant in neighborhood hospitality, and I reject any effort to criminalize tasteful reheating.
